text: Working with APIs is an important skill for modern developers. An API allows two programs to communicate with each other. To get data, your application sends HTTP requests, usually using methods like GET or POST. Most APIs return information in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Before you can use an API, you often need authentication, such as an API key or a token, to prove who you are. Many services also set rate limits, so you cannot send too many requests in a short time. Finally, good error handling is essential: always check status codes and prepare for problems like network failures or invalid responses.
